name: Cooper Companies

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (The Cooper Companies logo.png, 670x149 px)

description: Cooper owns two businesses. CooperVision (67 percent of sales) makes soft contact lenses sold to eye-care professionals and retailers; it is the profit engine, with a 27 percent operating margin. CooperSurgical (33 percent) sells fertility products and services (IVF consumables, donor eggs and sperm, genetic testing) and women's-health devices such as the Paragard contraceptive IUD, but earned only a 3 percent margin in FY2025 after $178M of amortisation, write-offs and severance. Contact lenses are a repeat-purchase consumable.

employees.note: "a workforce of more than 15,000"; 52 percent Americas, 42 percent EMEA, 6 percent Asia Pacific

businessLines.name: CooperVision
businessLines.how: Sells daily, two-week and monthly contact lenses (spherical, toric, multifocal, MiSight myopia control) to eye-care professionals and retailers; patients re-buy lenses daily or monthly.

businessLines.name: CooperSurgical
businessLines.how: Sells fertility consumables and services (IVF media, donor gametes, genomic testing) to clinics and women's-health devices to OB/GYN offices, hospitals and surgery centres; some storage services bill on a recurring basis.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-10-31), segment operating income (after inventory and long-lived asset write-offs and severance)

brands.name: MiSight 1 day
brands.note: first and only FDA-approved lens for slowing myopia in children aged 8-12 (2019); approved in Japan August 2025; no revenue disclosed

brands.name: Paragard
brands.note: contraceptive IUD in CooperSurgical office and surgical; no revenue disclosed
